source.title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences

accepted.question_text: In the House Allocation problem with strict or tied applicant preferences, can one obtain a better approximation algorithm for finding a matching of minimum unpopularity factor or minimum unpopularity margin, or alternatively prove tighter inapproximability bounds for these optimization problems?
accepted.context_brief: least unpopular matchings in house allocation

evidence.quote: future work could explore least unpopular matchings further by finding a better approximation algorithm or proving a tighter inapproximability bound.

accepted.question_text: Under the compact-indifference model of uncertain preferences, what is the computational complexity of computing the probability that a given matching is stable in a Stable Marriage instance?
accepted.context_brief: stable matching probability under compact indifference

accepted.question_text: Under the lottery model of uncertain preferences, what is the computational complexity of computing a matching with the highest probability of being stable in a Stable Marriage instance?
accepted.context_brief: highest-probability stable matching under lottery uncertainty

accepted.question_text: After the complexity gaps in Table 1 are resolved for Pareto-optimal and stable matchings under uncertain preferences, determine the analogous complexity of computing or reasoning about popular matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

accepted.question_text: After the complexity gaps in Table 1 are resolved for Pareto-optimal and stable matchings under uncertain preferences, determine the analogous complexity of computing or reasoning about rank-maximal matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

accepted.question_text: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, what is the complexity and algorithmic structure of allowing exchange cycles longer than length 2, rather than restricting exchanges to swaps only?
accepted.context_brief: longer exchange cycles in social-network house allocation

evidence.quote: The most striking open question regarding exchanges in social networks involves longer cycles instead of swaps only.

accepted.question_text: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, which exchange mechanisms are strategyproof, and under what structural restrictions on the network or exchange rules can strategyproofness be achieved?

evidence.quote: Strategyproofness is another topic worthy of investigation.

accepted.question_text: For the NP-hard cases of deciding reachability of a matching and finding a Pareto-optimal reachable matching in house allocation via swaps on a social network, what fixed-parameter or other parameterized algorithms are possible?
accepted.context_brief: parameterized complexity for hard social-network exchange cases

evidence.quote: Also, the hard cases in Theorems 5 and 6 could be tackled from a parameterised complexity viewpoint.

accepted.question_text: For each instance size n of the Stable Marriage problem, determine the maximum possible number x_n of stable matchings over all size-n instances, or at least substantially narrow the remaining gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on x_n.

evidence.quote: This open problem, first posed by Gusfield and Irving [45], concerns finding the maximum number xn of stable matchings admitted by any sm instance of size n.

accepted.question_text: Given a Stable Marriage instance I and an arbitrary matching M0, decide the complexity of determining whether the divorce digraph D_I contains a path from the vertex v_{M0} to some sink vertex, equivalently to a stable matching.
accepted.context_brief: reachability of stable matchings in the divorce digraph

evidence.quote: This leads to a natural open question, namely to resolve the complexity of the following decision problem: given an sm instance I and a matching M0, is there a path in DI from vM0 to a sink vertex?

accepted.question_text: For unrestricted Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists, close the approximability gap for finding a maximum-cardinality stable matching between the current best lower and upper bounds.
accepted.context_brief: approximability gap for unrestricted max smti

evidence.quote: These upper and lower bounds for general max smti remain the best known to date, and it is an open problem to close the gap between them.

accepted.question_text: For the one-sided-ties restriction 1s-max smti, can the current best approximation upper bound be improved all the way down to 5/4?
accepted.context_brief: improving the approximation ratio for 1s-max smti

evidence.quote: It is thus an open problem as to whether this latter upper bound can be reduced to 5/4 in the case of 1s-max smti.

accepted.question_text: When one or both sides of a Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists instance are derived from master lists, can those structural constraints be exploited to obtain better approximation guarantees for maximum-cardinality stable matching?

evidence.quote: it is an open question as to whether improved upper bounds exist in the presence of master lists on one or both sides.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an efficient output-sensitive algorithm that, given an instance I of Stable Marriage with Ties of size n, lists all stable matchings in time O(p(n) + |S_I| q(n)) for some polynomials p and q?
accepted.context_brief: enumerating all stable matchings in smt

evidence.quote: it is an open problem as to whether there is an efficient algorithm for listing all stable matchings, given an instance I of smt of size n. By efficient, we mean that the algorithm should have complexity O(p(n) + |SI|q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions.

accepted.question_text: For a uniformly random Stable Roommates instance of size n, determine the probability p_n that the instance admits a stable matching, especially its asymptotic behavior as n grows large.
accepted.context_brief: solvability probability for random stable roommates

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem, formulated as Problem 8 in Gusfield and Irving [45], is the computation of pn, the probability that a random instance, chosen uniformly from all possible sr instances of size n, admits a stable matching. Of particular interest is the asymptotic behaviour of pn, as n grows large.

accepted.question_text: For the more general notion of an (a,b)-supermatch in Stable Roommates or Stable Marriage settings, is the decision problem in NP, and if so what is its precise computational complexity?
accepted.context_brief: complexity of deciding existence of general (a,b)-supermatches

evidence.quote: However, for the more general case of (a, b)-supermatches, it is not even known whether the problem belongs to NP.

accepted.question_text: For a given Stable Roommates instance, what approximation guarantees are achievable for finding a (1,b)-supermatch that minimizes the repair parameter b?
accepted.context_brief: approximability of minimizing b for supermatches

evidence.quote: Genc et al. [41] also provided two metaheuristics for finding a (1, b)-supermatch for a given sri instance that minimises the value of b, however, the approximability of this problem has not been studied theoretically.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, including definitions, existence questions, and algorithms, under robustness notions analogous to those already studied for stable marriage and stable marriage with incomplete lists.
accepted.context_brief: robust stable matchings in stable roommates

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, robust stable matchings in sr have not been studied previously (either in the senses of Mai and Vazirani [66, 67] or Chen et al. [26]).

accepted.question_text: Can the current O(N^5) upper bound for computing the weighted straight skeleton of a polygon be improved, perhaps by exploiting additional structure in the associated Stable Roommates instance used by the reduction?

evidence.quote: They conjectured that this running time can be improved. A deeper insight into the structure of the underlying sr instance might lead to such an improvement in the efficiency of the algorithm.
